newsitem.title: USA: Judge rules Pamela Lee did not break contract.
newsitem.headline: Judge rules Pamela Lee did not break contract.

text.p: A judge ruled Tuesday in favor of actress Pamela Lee in a $5 million breach of contract suit, saying there was no binding agreement when she pulled out of a movie deal.
In a written judgment, Judge David Horowitz said the former "Baywatch" TV star did not break a contract when she changed her mind about making a cable TV movie "Hello, She Lied".
The judge said the film-makers, The Private Movie Co., failed to prove "by a preponderance of evidence" that Lee entered into a contract to make the film.
The company had sued her for $5 million, claiming she broke a contract because she was offered a better deal to make a feature film, "Barb Wire".

The actress, who is married to rock drummer Tommy Lee of Motley Crue, said during testimony in the non-jury trial this month that she pulled out of the project because she objected to graphic sex scenes in the proposed film.

The movie-makers, who claimed to have lost millions of dollars as a result of Lee backing out, said the actress had an oral agreement to make the movie. But it also acknowledged that a written agreement was never executed.
